raw_title: Locally-Made Mercedes-Benz Electric GLC Launched At Rs. 78.50 Lakh
title: Locally-Made Mercedes-Benz Electric GLC Launched At Rs. 78.50 Lakh
raw_summary: GaadiWaadi - The GLC 400 4Matic Electric becomes the first locally built Mercedes-Benz based on the MB.EA-M platform as Pune joins Bremen in its global production network Mercedes-Benz India has started local production of the all-new Electric GLC at its Chakan facility in Pune, Maharashtra. The first locally assembled unit is the GLC 400 4Matic Electric, which carries an ex-showroom price of Rs. 78.50 lakh across India. Deliveries are scheduled to commence in mid-November 2026, placing the electric SUV at the centre of the company’s next phase of local manufacturing. The Electric GLC brings two major technology firsts to the Indian production facility. It is the first locally manufactured Mercedes-Benz based on the MB.EA-M electric vehicle architecture and also the first locally built model to use the Mercedes-Benz Operating System, or MB.OS. The Pune facility is only the second plant globally to manufacture this generation of the Electric GLC, following the company’s factory in Bremen, Germany. The production milestone was marked in the presence of Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis, Sunetra Pawar and senior Mercedes-Benz Group executives, including Chairman Ola Källenius and CTO Joerg Burzer. The company says the Electric GLC is assembled on the same flexible production line used for combustion-engine vehicles. This arrangement allows the Pune plant to handle electric and petrol or diesel models on a shared manufacturing line. Mercedes-Benz India has committed an additional Rs. 200 crore investment in 2026 towards manufacturing operations, new product start up activities and digitisation. Its cumulative investment in India now stands at Rs. 3,200 crore, which the company describes as the highest among luxury carmakers in the country. Mercedes-Benz also says it has sold more than 2.4 lakh vehicles locally, another record figure for a luxury manufacturer in India. The new model also introduces the MB.OS digital platform to locally manufactured Mercedes-Benz vehicles. The operating system is designed to integrate vehicle functions and digital services, although the Indian press release does not detail the full feature list or equipment specifications of the GLC 400 4Matic Electric. The company positions the model as a combination of its established GLC design and comfort attributes and its newer electric and software technologies. Mercedes-Benz India is also changing the charging benefit offered to new electric vehicle customers. Instead of a complimentary AC wall box, buyers will receive MB.Charge public charging credits. The company has not specified the credit value or the duration of the benefit in the announcement. This change forms part of the ownership offering alongside the locally manufactured electric SUV. The start of Electric GLC production gives the Pune facility a more prominent role in Mercedes-Benz’s global electric vehicle manufacturing network. The company has highlighted the plant’s flexible production capability and the contribution of its workforce to the model’s production ramp up.

title: High gas prices are pumping up used EV sales: these are FLYING off the lot
raw_summary: A new car affordability crisis and punishing gas prices are driving an unprecedented number of used car buyers to consider going electric, and that increased demand without a corresponding increase in supply means these used EVs are flying off dealer lots. Days on the lot. That’s dealer-speak for the average number of days a given vehicle typically sits in inventory before finding a buyer. That’s critically important to dealers, since the vehicles on their lots are commonly financed through something called floorplan credit, and every additional day a car spends on a dealer’s lot can mean another day of interest payments and another day closer to a curtailment . Days on the lot can be even more important to dealers when it comes to cars owned outright, as well, as the dealers can have significant cash tied up in vehicles they’ve purchased outright, and every day those cars sit is another day that money isn’t working for them elsewhere.

Days on the lot. That’s dealer-speak for the average number of days a given vehicle typically sits in inventory before finding a buyer. That’s critically important to dealers, since the vehicles on their lots are commonly financed through something called floorplan credit, and every additional day a car spends on a dealer’s lot can mean another day of interest payments and another day closer to a curtailment . Days on the lot can be even more important to dealers when it comes to cars owned outright, as well, as the dealers can have significant cash tied up in vehicles they’ve purchased outright, and every day those cars sit is another day that money isn’t working for them elsewhere.
That’s what makes this month’s fastest-selling used EVs particularly interesting, because these used EVs aren’t just selling fast for electric vehicles – they’re selling fast, period .

Dealer news sources Automotive News and Cox Automotive report that the average new car spent 82 days on the lot in October, with a 75-day target being an industry-wide benchmark. At the same time, the Audi Q4 Sportback e-tron Quattro with its 258-mile EPA-estimated range is turning in just 29.8 days. (!)

That Audi’s not alone. In a recently-released vehicle pricing study , iSeeCars reported that the Toyota BZ4x , Lexus RZ300e , Honda Prologue , and Borrás-family favorite Polestar 2 are all turning in an average of 35 days or less, with the BMW i4, iX , Kia EV6 , and Chevrolet Equinox EV just a day or two behind.

“The results reveal a market where EVs are appreciating in average asking price much faster than other drivetrains, while also spending less time waiting for buyers,” said iSeeCars Executive Analyst Karl Brauer, who found that average transaction prices for EVs rose 9.8% last month as ICE-powered vehicles stayed steady, rising just 0.3%. “Hybrids are experiencing moderate improvements in price and selling speed, while gasoline-powered vehicles have seen their selling times increase,” he adds, “despite relatively stable prices.”
Used electric vehicles averaged a price of $32,533 in September 2026, up $2,896 from the $29,637 ATP recorded a year earlier.

title: First: Volvo CE Electric equipment does the work, without disturbing the wildlife
raw_summary: For the first time, electric equipment assets are being put to work in the National Wildlife Refuge System, where a battery-powered, zero-emission ECR25 Electric compact excavator and L25 Electric compact wheel loader made by Volvo CE are making the wild more accessible to everyone. Construction work isn’t exactly welcome in the wilderness – between diesel exhaust, engine noises, and the constant rumble of heavy machinery, even a relatively small project can have a big impact on the native wildlife. To minimize that impact, US Fish and Wildlife Service is turning to Volvo CE and its compact excavators and wheel loaders to get the job done, building out a new, ADA accessible trail in Virginia’s Occoquan Bay National Wildlife Refuge.

Construction work isn’t exactly welcome in the wilderness – between diesel exhaust, engine noises, and the constant rumble of heavy machinery, even a relatively small project can have a big impact on the native wildlife. To minimize that impact, US Fish and Wildlife Service is turning to Volvo CE and its compact excavators and wheel loaders to get the job done, building out a new, ADA accessible trail in Virginia’s Occoquan Bay National Wildlife Refuge.

“We are excited to partner with the US Fish and Wildlife Service on this project to demonstrate Volvo’s commitment to lowering emissions and working to build the future we all want and need,” said Dr. Ray Gallant, VP of Product Management and Productivity, Volvo CE. “Projects like the one at the Occoquan Bay National Wildlife Refuge give a glimpse of how electric machines can create a more climate-friendly future for the construction industry.”

The refuge is home to a diverse array of grasslands, wetlands, and woods that attract red foxes, painted turtles, osprey, river otters, and countless other rarely seen species – and the ADA accessible path being laid down by the L25 Electric compact wheel loader will allow wheelchair-bound visitors to travel a half-mile-long trail around one of the pond . Meanwhile, the ECR25 Electric compact excavator will be digging trenches to improve drainage from the pond and helping to place a viewing platform that extends out over the water.
Keeping the machines running is a portable EV ARC solar-powered charging system from Beam Global that’s designed to drive down the project’s carbon footprint even further.

article_paragraphs: On Wednesday, NASA's Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory , a space telescope that's been in orbit since 2004, finally re-entered Earth's atmosphere above Indonesia. However, it appears to have done so with a risk of casualties five times beyond what NASA technical standards mandate. How and why this happened isn't immediately clear; NASA Public Affairs Specialist Alise Fisher told Jalopnik, "In the leadup to Swift's Nov. 20, 2004, launch, NASA determined the risk was consistent with mission requirements as allowed by agency policy." Somewhere between launch and reentry, that risk assessment shifted. It's unlikely that anybody made a specific mistake; this is probably the result of, well, space being hard. Still, it does highlight that our main defense against the detritus of astronomical ambitions is pure luck.

Swift is only crashing to Earth because it ran out of fuel to stay in orbit or adjust its trajectory. To NASA's credit, it did throw $30 million at a private company in an unprecedented attempt to rescue Swift with another satellite that would pull it back up into safe orbit. Sadly, the rescue satellite itself failed, dooming Swift to this fate.

In formal terms, Swift suffered an "uncontrolled reentry," which basically means it had no propulsion and just fell from space. NASA's own requirements, most recently updated in 2021 but going all the way back to 2001, state: "For uncontrolled reentry, the risk of human casualty from surviving debris shall be less than 0.0001 (1:10,000)." If you're not aware, there's no actual law requiring that satellites de-orbit in some sort of safe way that won't, you know, crash into a city or kill anyone. So our shield against the skies is just statistics. This is the threshold at which NASA feels the risk is acceptable. For reference, in all of history, just about 10,000 satellites have de-orbited , so... statistically we're due. And that was before we were putting tens of thousands of satellites up every few years .

In Swift's instance, however, NASA played its cards a little close to its chest. For one thing, it did not put out a risk assessment for the reentry , which is unusual. Then, in the middle of a longer announcement , the agency mentioned that Swift's risk of human casualties was actually "1 in 2,100." That's a risk of human injury or death five times beyond what it was meant to be.

Fortunately, the odds appear to have resolved in our favor. There are no reports of anyone being struck by space debris from Swift. Most of the satellite was expected to burn up during reentry; the trouble would come from whatever survived, likely dense pieces like the telescope lens or the reaction wheels. If any of those made it to the surface, there doesn't appear to have been a person around it.

That's a roll of the dice, though. At some point, as thousands of satellites de-orbit per year in our new megaconstellation era, laws should be passed to manage this formally. That would likely mean requiring controlled reentries, when the satellite still has a little fuel left to navigate to a safe spot out in the ocean. The other option, which companies like SpaceX have been pursuing, is to design the satellite to burn up entirely on reentry. The issue there is what effect all that vaporized metal might have on the atmosphere. Scientists don't yet know the answer, for the simple reason that there was never a reason to ask that question before. Now, the health of our planet may depend on it.

As space gets busier and busier, more and more will fall to us down here from up there. Up until now, the power of statistics has kept us safe. But eventually, a 1 in 10,000 chance is going to happen. Especially if some of those chances turn out to be riskier than intended.

title: China's Buick Electra GS Is A Stylish Hybrid America Can't Have
raw_summary: Buick hasn't offered a sedan in the U.S. since sales of the Regal ended in 2020. But it's a totally different story in China, where SUV haters can choose from multiple low-riding four-door cars, including the handsome, electrified Electra L7. Now, Buick's Chinese division is gearing up to launch its Electra GS little brother, and you have to wonder if America is missing out. Details of the Electra GS were revealed by China's Ministry of Industry and Information Technology filings ahead of the official debut, and they tell us the production car has changed quite a bit since GM showed the Electra GS concept (below) at the Shanghai Auto Show in 2025. The LED headlights have been inverted, and the Buick badge moved from the hood to a front facia that features less body-color plastic. The concept was incredibly handsome, but maybe looked a little too much like a Tesla Model 3 around the front. The production car looks less like a Tesla, but sacrifices some eye candy points.

article_paragraphs: Buick hasn't offered a sedan in the U.S. since sales of the Regal ended in 2020. But it's a totally different story in China, where SUV haters can choose from multiple low-riding four-door cars, including the handsome, electrified Electra L7. Now, Buick's Chinese division is gearing up to launch its Electra GS little brother, and you have to wonder if America is missing out.

Details of the Electra GS were revealed by China's Ministry of Industry and Information Technology filings ahead of the official debut, and they tell us the production car has changed quite a bit since GM showed the Electra GS concept (below) at the Shanghai Auto Show in 2025. The LED headlights have been inverted, and the Buick badge moved from the hood to a front facia that features less body-color plastic. The concept was incredibly handsome, but maybe looked a little too much like a Tesla Model 3 around the front. The production car looks less like a Tesla, but sacrifices some eye candy points.

An imminent ban on pop-out door handles in China meant the concept's had to go, and though the fastback profile is carried across, the show car's traditional sedan trunk has made way for a more practical hatch. The taillights are also new, and so is the "Buick" lettering spelled out at the rear of the car.

Another genuinely massive change is the productions GS's massive reduction in scale. MIIT data shows it's 196.1 inches (4,980 mm) long, but the concept (pictured above) was a huge 208.7 inches (5,300 mm). Same thing with wheelbase. The concept's axles were 126 inches (3,200 mm) apart, but the production GS wheelbase measures 112.8 inches (2,865 mm), making the finished car similar in size to a Toyota Crown , rather than a Mercedes S-Class.

The biggest switch of all, though, takes place under the hood. GM didn't reveal much in the way of technical details about the concept, but it did confirm it was a fully electric car that rode on a dedicated EV platform, giving a totally flat floor. But, like Adam West's 1966 Batman jumping on the Batpoles inside Wayne Manor dressed in a comfy cardigan, and emerging inside the Batcave in full caped crusader garb 100 ft (31 m) down, the GS bound for dealers has arrived for duty as a plug-in hybrid.

Base cars pair a 97 horsepower (98 PS) naturally aspirated 1.5-liter inline-4 with a 221 hp (224 PS) electric motor, but a more expensive variant swaps the NA gas motor for a turbocharged version of the same, making 154 hp (156 PS). We'll have wait for the full China debut to find out more about the GS, including whether the interior looks anything like the concept's (below). But don't pin your hopes on seeing that yoke steering wheel — we can already see a conventional steering wheel is present in the studio images of the exterior.

Back in the U.S., GM's sales have been hurt by its lack of hybrid offerings. The automaker was so sure EVs would dominate the car market by the end of the decade that it didn't bother developing them, except for the Corvette E-Ray (now renamed Grand Sport X). Rival brands like Toyota and Hyundai hedged their bets, and made both, and are now reaping the rewards, while GM is rushing to catch up toward the end of the decade.

Could the GS work here? Absolutely, but it's not likely. GM does import vehicles from China, including Chinese-built Buick Envision from China , although production of that model is due to shift to Kansas in 2028. Complicating matters is the fact that the GS is the result of a joint venture between GM and China's SAIC, and new restrictions on Chinese software that take effect with the 2027 model year would make it tricky to get this car compliant for the U.S. market, even if production was shifted to North America to avoid tariffs. Overall, we'd say don't hold your breath for this Buick.

article_paragraphs: General Motors (GM) issued a recall affecting more than 67,000 Cadillac and Chevy EVs because a software glitch can cause a temporary loss of braking.
The recall comes after a 2024 Cadillac Lyriq ran into a garage (at a low speed). On April 10, 2026, a GM tech expert submitted a report to GM’s Speak Up for Safety (SUFS) program for review.

After internal testing, GM was able to replicate the glitch, similar to a recall it issued in 2024. GM said the issue stems from a software glitch with the brake system control module (BSCM) that can cause a temporary loss of braking while driving under certain conditions.
When drivers lightly tap the brakes during a sharp turn and the vehicle hits a bump, the software’s slip calculation may misinterpret wheel movement.
In some instances, it can lead to a temporary loss of braking. The glitch only affects pAWD vehicles, including certain Cadillac Lyriq, Celestiq, Vistiq, and Chevy Blazer EV.
In a letter sent to the NHTSA on October 29, GM said the recall impacted 67,380 vehicles total, including certain:
According to documents filed with the NHTSA, GM found 24 field complaints related to the issue. Of these, 20 involved minor accidents, and two involved allegations of minor injuries.
The complaints were received between February 24, 2024, and June 11, 2026. GM said it has implemented software corrections in production over the past few months.

“Chasing Gold” is powered by a 427 LS V-8 with a 2.9-liter Whipple supercharger. A Bowler 4L80E transmission sends power through a GSI chassis to a Currie 9-inch rear end. Auto Metal Direct sheet metal and custom fabrication from Arizona Custom Car Design shaped the squarebody of the truck, while Kolor Koalition developed its custom blue paint. The front grille features custom “His” badging.

“Sweet Emotion” takes a different approach, with a Stage 2 LS3 V-8 topped by a Granatelli Motorsports Zilla intake manifold. It rides on a Roadster Shop chassis and also uses a Bowler 4L80E transmission and Currie 9-inch rear end. Arizona Custom Car Design handled the bodywork and collaborated with Kolor Koalition on the Blazer’s purple finish. Of course, the custom “hers” badging is on the front of this one.

Both Chevrolets have gold trim, Variant wheels, Dakota Digital instrumentation, and Rockford Fosgate audio systems. Apex Leather supplied leather for both vehicles. Arizona Custom Car Design built the C10’s interior, while Ciadella Interiors completed the K5’s cabin. Their flannel company, Dixxon Flannel Co., is branded throughout the cabin, including their custom flannel on the seats and logo on the dashboards.
The pair brings together a long list of aftermarket companies, but the builds share a clear theme: classic Chevrolet squarebody design, updated with LS power and modern components.

raw_title: Almost no one uses AI agents to book their Uber, company says
title: Almost no one uses AI agents to book their Uber, company says
raw_summary: Very few people are using personal AI agents to order Ubers, apparently. On the transportation giant’s third-quarter earnings call on Wednesday, the company said that only four rides were ordered through an AI agent during its busiest week in October: the week of Halloween. While more people used an AI agent to order food through its delivery service, Uber Eats, the volume was still fairly small compared to the overall number of trips.

article_paragraphs: Very few people are using personal AI agents to order Ubers, apparently. On the transportation giant’s third-quarter earnings call on Wednesday, the company said that only four rides were ordered through an AI agent during its busiest week in October: the week of Halloween.
While more people used an AI agent to order food through its delivery service, Uber Eats, the volume was still fairly small compared to the overall number of trips.

Uber’s chief financial officer, Balaji Krishnamurthy, told Wall Street analysts on the call that the company handled around 320 million trips and orders across Uber and Uber Eats during the week of Halloween, but only 500 Uber Eats orders were placed by an AI agent.

“It is very, very early and very limited traction that we are seeing so far,” said CEO Dara Khosrowshahi, referring to the low number of orders placed by AI agents. “Listen, we hope that there will be more traction.”

The surprisingly low numbers of AI-initiated transactions come amid growing hype for a new wave of AI agents that don’t just answer questions but also handle tasks on users’ behalf. There’s been an explosion of personal AI startups, including one of the buzziest, Instinct, which was founded last year and raised its most recent round of funding at a $10 billion valuation. Meta’s Muse also became the No. 1 app in Apple’s U.S. App Store last month, topping 10 million users, per Meta’s own reporting . The company said many were using it to shop and transact with businesses.
OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and SpaceXAI (Grok) are also now offering their own AI agents, as are numerous smaller startups.

Still, early numbers from public companies indicate the agentic web still has a long way to go. DoorDash, for instance, said last week on its earnings call that it has only received a few hundred orders from AI agents so far, as most customers are still placing orders through the DoorDash app.

Uber is seeing the same behavior, it seems. Khosrowshahi pointed out that the average time to book a ride is only 50 seconds in the company’s app, and re-ordering a favorite food only takes 90 seconds. That suggests an AI agent isn’t necessarily saving anyone time.

But now Mercedes wants to give the bumper sticker a digital update by allowing you to turn your rear window into a pixelated message board.
article_paragraphs: Americans have been sending messages to the drivers behind them ever since Forest P. Gill turned a load of self-adhesive paper into the first bumper sticker in 1946. But now Mercedes wants to give the bumper sticker a digital update by allowing you to turn your rear window into a pixelated message board.

Mini LEDs embedded in the rear window light up when needed to create the messages, and they are invisible the rest of the time so as not to spoil the driver's view of what's going on behind him. This being Mercedes, the messages are not in the realm of "Why don't you act like your hairline and take a few steps back" or "My other car is a Mercedes." They're sensible, safety-focused, and hilariously passive aggressive.

Someone blasting you from behind with their high beams? Show them the headlight symbol with a massive red line through it. Tailgater trouble ? The "keep distance" message kindly suggests that back off a little. Other worthy possibilities include warnings of a pedestrian crossing or a crash ahead, or a signal that the car in front of them is about to back into a parking bay.

These are the officially sanctioned messages. Mercedes makes no mention of drivers being allowed to come up with their own, and probably for good reason. But you just know that it'll take about five minutes after this tech hits the streets for some enterprising coder to hack the system and deliver digital abuse to any following BMW, Audi or Lexus.

Mercedes' engineers haven't only been working out how to display messages on the rear window. They've been busy with the side windows and windshield, too, though the LEDs involved are understandably much smaller. We've had head-up displays for over 20 years, but instead of limiting displays to a small area in front of the driver, Mercedes wants to turn a large area of windshield into a giant communication surface. A projector in the top of the dashboard beams content upwards, and a transparent film laminated into the glass reflects the projected wavelengths using "holographic optical elements" (HOE). Hyundai showed something similar last year.

The light is bundled in such a way that the image can be seen in all conditions, including bright sunlight. But the clever part is that anything projected onto the passenger side of the glass can't be viewed by the driver, and vice versa. Which means passengers can watch videos and movies while the car is in motion. Whether they will, is another matter. Automakers have been pushing expensive passenger-side digital dashboard screens for the past few years, which you'd think would give a better viewing experience than this new projected tech, but one study found that they're rarely used .

Mercedes says other uses beyond entertainment include video calls and displaying points of interest along your route. That's likely to become a big deal in the years to come as businesses like restaurants, hotels and tourist attractions pay to appear as stop-off suggestions in cars from all brands . No timeframe was given for the tech's introduction, but if Mercedes is showing it, it must have production intent. Our guess is you'll be able to digitally tut-tut at the driver behind you before the end of the decade.

raw_title: Nabrawind’s Crane-Free Wind Towers Face a Supplier Test
title: Nabrawind's Crane-Free Wind Towers Face a Supplier Test
raw_summary: Spain’s Nabrawind has developed a way to install exceptionally tall wind turbine towers without bringing an enormous crawler crane to the site. Its Nabralift system uses a tubular upper tower supported by a three-legged steel structure. Hydraulic equipment raises the assembled turbine while modular sections are inserted below it near ground level. The lifting frame can then be removed and used on another installation. This addresses genuine logistical and construction problems, particularly at remote sites where specialist cranes are expensive to transport and where wind can interrupt conventional lifting operations. The company has progressed beyond demonstration-scale hardware. In September 2026, UL Solutions issued type certification for Envision’s 7.8 MW turbine on Nabrawind’s 188-meter tower. Fortescue is using 17 of those tower configurations at the 133 MW Nullagine wind project in Western Australia’s Pilbara region, where construction is underway. Nabrawind previously erected a 160-meter prototype in Spain in under two weeks and has supplied smaller commercial towers in Morocco and France.

Its Nabralift system uses a tubular upper tower supported by a three-legged steel structure. article_paragraphs: Spain’s Nabrawind has developed a way to install exceptionally tall wind turbine towers without bringing an enormous crawler crane to the site. Its Nabralift system uses a tubular upper tower supported by a three-legged steel structure. Hydraulic equipment raises the assembled turbine while modular sections are inserted below it near ground level. The lifting frame can then be removed and used on another installation. This addresses genuine logistical and construction problems, particularly at remote sites where specialist cranes are expensive to transport and where wind can interrupt conventional lifting operations.

The company has progressed beyond demonstration-scale hardware. In September 2026, UL Solutions issued type certification for Envision’s 7.8 MW turbine on Nabrawind’s 188-meter tower. Fortescue is using 17 of those tower configurations at the 133 MW Nullagine wind project in Western Australia’s Pilbara region, where construction is underway. Nabrawind previously erected a 160-meter prototype in Spain in under two weeks and has supplied smaller commercial towers in Morocco and France.

The engineering benefits are credible. Nabrawind reports using roughly 20% less tower steel than comparable conventional tubular designs and reducing foundation concrete by as much as 80%, depending on the design and site. Those are supplier claims rather than independently established savings across all wind farms. The potential to avoid large cranes, simplify transport and raise turbines in windier conditions could also matter substantially to total installed cost and construction schedules. High hub heights only earn their keep when those costs are justified by the electricity generated over the project’s life.

The current deployment has an unusual commercial structure. Fortescue acquired Nabrawind in September 2025 and is building Nullagine to serve its own mining operations. Fortescue has the capital, internal electricity demand and industrial incentive to support a technology it owns. Successful installation in that context would be important evidence of construction performance, but it would not establish that an unrelated wind developer can finance and maintain the same system under ordinary third-party commercial arrangements.

Nabralift’s proprietary construction approach creates a procurement issue. Conventional tubular towers can be sourced from several qualified manufacturers, and experienced contractors can compete for much of their construction work. A developer selecting Nabralift currently depends on one supplier for the core tower system, specialist lifting knowledge and associated support. Wind turbine original-equipment manufacturers also create supplier dependencies, but concentrating another critical part of the project in a proprietary installation system requires its own contract and risk assessment.

A type certificate provides valuable technical assurance about the certified turbine-and-tower configuration. A lender or insurer still needs enforceable delivery schedules, long-term warranties, repair and maintenance provisions, clarity on replacement parts, and a workable remedy if the supplier’s capacity or commercial priorities change. These questions become more important when a wind farm must operate for 25 years or longer and there is no qualified alternative provider of the same system.

Nabrawind’s next important proof point is an independently developed and financed large wind farm that accepts those risks on commercial terms. Qualified installation partners, credible long-term service arrangements and greater competitive capacity could make its engineering advantages easier for developers to buy. The 188-meter tower has earned technical attention; its broader market depends on financing and procurement confidence catching up with the machinery.

My full TFIE Strategy Briefing assessment examines Nabrawind’s self-erecting design, Fortescue’s Nullagine deployment and the supplier concentration that independent wind developers would have to manage. It follows my earlier assessment of 300-meter wind towers , where construction economics were the central challenge.

raw_title: Rimac Is Helping BMW Create Two New Mystery Models
title: Rimac Is Helping BMW Create Two New Mystery Models
raw_summary: Rimac has transformed from a small Croatian brand that built just eight examples of the wild Concept One into a technology and manufacturing juggernaut that now owns Bugatti. When it's not building hypercars, Rimac supplies electric drivetrains to some of the industry's top automotive brands, and boss Mate Rimac has confirmed it's working on two more cars with BMW. The new i7 is the first model from BMW to use a jointly developed battery system created alongside Rimac. This system combines the German automaker's Gen6 4695 lithium-ion cylindrical cells with its Gen5 module-based technology into a scalable architecture that other vehicles can use. Rimac manufactures the battery system at its campus near Zagreb. In a recent interview with Auto News , Mate Rimac confirmed that "there are two more cars in the pipeline" being developed alongside BMW. Details about these new models haven't been announced, so we can only speculate. New products from BMW's Neue Klasse line-up seem most likely.

In the same interview, Rimac shared how it landed an important supply contract with BMW. He gave BMW executives a tour of the Rimac Campus while it was still in the early stages of construction, and pointed out where he planned to establish a production line for BMW at the site. The German automaker said it had no contracts with Rimac.

"It doesn't matter," Mate Rimac replied, "I'm building it for you," reassuring the German brand that Rimac was committed to the project. "BMW is premium," he added. "You have to be the best technically and commercially to supply them. They have to be competitive on the market and they cannot pay a premium to get components from a company that's not optimized. To win that business, we had to be better than everyone on the market both technically and commercially."

A wide range of cars feature Rimac technology. These include the Koenigsegg Regera, Aston Martin Valkyrie, Porsche 911 GTS T-Hybrid, and the new Ceer EVs from Saudi Arabia . In September, a consortium of investors purchased Porsche's 21% shareholding in Rimac Group and its 45% stake in the Bugatti Rimac joint venture. Free from Porsche's influence, Rimac says it can now make decisions faster. "A big company like Porsche is always risk aware and risk averse, and the decision-making process is long", Mate Rimac said. "Now I can sit down with my management team, make a decision and go. Something that would have taken six months to decide waiting for board approvals gets done much quicker."

raw_summary: Mercedes-Benz is delaying the start of its U.S. production of the GLC-class crossover, according to Automotive News . The automaker had originally planned for production of the GLC to begin in late 2027, but the paper reports that it has now been delayed to 2030. When the U.S. production does begin, it will take place at the automaker’s Vance, Alabama, plant. According to the AN report, Mercedes is delaying the move in production to wait for the arrival of the next-generation GLC-class. “Investing in the plant for about half a life cycle and then having to retool for the next-generation GLC doesn’t make a lot of sense financially,” Sam Fiorani, the vice president of AutoForecast, told the outlet. The Alabama plant, in its current configuration, is home to the GLS-class and GLE-class SUVs, along with their electric counterparts.

article_paragraphs: Police in L.A. aren't messing around anymore when it comes to street takeovers

Last week, we told you how deputies in Los Angeles County managed to shut down a couple of street takeovers before they started . This week, we're learning that the task force there appears eager to make sure that wasn't a one-hit wonder. Authorities say a group traveled from Northern California for more illegal events over the weekend. Seven cars now have a month-long stay at the impound lot.

According to the Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department, the gatherings went by "Bay to LA." Its Street Takeover Task Force conducted several enforcement operations, making 22 arrests and issuing 74 citations. Another 22 vehicles received citations requiring state referee inspections. As we've also noted in the past, those inspections can completely shift the way a person approaches the future of their car use. The LASD didn't provide a list of what cars were impounded, but it did post a video to social media , which gives us a good indication. Included in the video are an SN95 Ford Mustang convertible, a similarly aged Chevrolet Camaro, a Pontiac G8, at least one Chevy SS, and a third-gen Lexus LS.

The alleged offenses included reckless driving , exhibition of speed, driving with a suspended license, felony evading, felony illegal firearms possession, and felony conspiracy to commit reckless driving. Deputies worked in Carson, Cerritos, Compton, Lynwood, Commerce, Lakewood, and unincorporated parts of the county.

Interestingly, there's a couple of patterns emerging here. Yes, last week, police cracked down on two takeovers, but how they did so is key. Authorities specifically credited their ability to see these events advertised on social media for helping them do their job. During that operation, police arrested another 22 people, issued 104 citations, and handed out 55 emission or exhaust violations.

This time around, it seems like the organizers once again posted about the event online before showing up. Will they keep doing that? If so, it appears as though police will be paying attention and ready to show up and shut things down.

Officers in California don't just treat drivers as participants. Occupants of the vehicle in question can end up with charges too if that vehicle is participating in the takeover. In fact, the law goes even further. Police can cite those who use their own vehicles to block an intersection even if they're not doing donuts or anything of the sort. Then, there are the spectators who can also end up with citations. That's right, just being at the scene can result in significant financial penalties.

The Temerario might be the runt of the Lamborghini supercar litter, but it's still one raging bull. Taking the reins from its widely lauded Huracan predecessor, the Temerario is the least expensive way into Lambo's supercar lineup, but it doesn’t sacrifice much performance compared to the company's Revuelto flagship—in fact, it beats its brawnier older brother to 60 mph by a tenth of a second.

Under the Temerario's origami-folded sheetmetal lies a newly developed 4.0-liter twin-turbo V-8 nestled into the car's aluminum spaceframe just ahead of the rear axle. As if 789 horsepower from the engine alone wasn’t enough, a trio of electric motors—one mounted between the engine and transmission and one at each front wheel—ups its total output to 907 Italian stallions. If you somehow tire of the sound of the flat-plane-crank V-8's goosebump-raising 10,000-rpm wail, the electric motors also allow for short periods of silent, all-electric driving. With its mighty hybrid-assisted thrust, poster-worthy looks, and agile moves, the Temerario is every inch a purebred Lambo and well worthy of supercar status.

Lamborghini's newest bull debuted in 2026 and charges into 2027 without any notable changes.

If this year's model is largely unchanged and you're comfortable with a lightly used car, you may want to consider shopping previous model years. A one-to-three-year-old model will likely have a warranty and it'll cost less than buying new.

The Temerario's powertrain consists of a twin-turbo 4.0-liter V-8 with a flat-plane crankshaft, a trio of axial-flux electric motors, and an eight-speed dual-clutch transmission. The Temerario's V-8 alone is good for 789 horsepower; adding the output of the three electric motors brings the total combined output to 907 horsepower. That's just 94 ponies shy of the Lamborghini Revuelto , the brand's V-12 halo car. On the Temerario, one electric motor mounts to the V-8 in front of the transmission, while the remaining two live up front, one at each wheel. The Temerario's V-8 redlines at 10,000 rpm, and the engine's peak torque of 538 pound-feet is available from 4000 to 7000 rpm. While the flat-plane-crank V-8 sounds glorious when pushed to its limit, we wish that its exhaust packed a bit more fury earlier in the rev range.

In order to honor their longtime collaboration, Kia created a special sculpture by blending traditional styling clay with tennis court clay from Monte Carlo, Paris, Rome, and Madrid.

To break up the monotony of the orange material, Kia used white design tape to highlight the character lines of the EV4 GT. These accents double as a reference to the white tennis court lines and are joined by custom exterior graphics highlighting Nadal's major career milestones.

A walk around the sculpture will remind Nadal of his clay-related achievements. At the front, Kia printed "63 TITLES ON CLAY" next to the headlight and "81 CONSECUTIVE WINS ON CLAY" on the hood. The profile carries a note about the "4 FRENCH OPEN TITLES" at Roland-Garros out of Nadal's 22 Grand Slam single titles. Finally, the rear end has his signature next to "5 SEASONS AT NUMBER 1" lettering.

The unique Kia EV4 was presented to the tennis legend at his Rafa Nadal Academy in Mallorca, Spain. It has the same footprint as the production EV4 GT hatchback, but is non-drivable and doesn't have an interior. Still, it rides on production wheels and tires, so it likely rolls. Most clay models sit on special platforms with cart wheels, making it easier to move them around in tight spaces.

While Kia could have chosen a higher-end model, like the electric Stinger successor, over a compact electric hatchback for the tribute, the eye-catching material and tennis references will certainly make it a great conversation starter in Nadal's garage. After all, the "King of Clay" should have a car made of clay in his collection.

"For more than twenty years, Kia has been by my side throughout my career, through all the highs and the challenges," said Nadal . "Receiving this tribute, created from the material that has defined so much of my journey, is incredibly meaningful. It is a special reminder of everything we have shared, and I am honored by this gesture."

The automaker noted that despite the increasing use of digital tools in automotive design , clay modeling remains an integral part of vehicle development as it allows designers to judge "proportions, surfaces, finishes, and tensions" on a physical product.

raw_title: Tesla Allegedly Misled Thousands Of South Korean Customers About 'Full Self-Driving'
title: Tesla Allegedly Misled Thousands Of South Korean Customers About 'Full Self-Driving
raw_summary: Usually, when we tell you that Tesla has gotten into hot water for misleading folks about its "Full Self-Driving" Level 2 driver assistance system , it has to do with Tesla overstating just how capable of a system it is. That's not the case in South Korea, though, where the Texas-based automaker has allegedly vastly overstated the legality of FSD usage and charged customers for it nonetheless. Now, tens of thousands of Korean Tesla owners are looking for answers. Tesla apparently markets FSD in South Korea despite the fact that it knows the majority of its cars can't legally use the program in the country, the complaint from an advocacy group alleges. That means it can't be activated on the car. Soon, the complaint will be filed with the Korean Fair Trade Commission, a consumer protection agency, according to Reuters . Tesla will have to answer for why it marketed FSD to prospective buyers for years, even collecting the $6,726 lump-sum payment required for activation, even though it couldn't legally be used.

article_paragraphs: Usually, when we tell you that Tesla has gotten into hot water for misleading folks about its "Full Self-Driving" Level 2 driver assistance system , it has to do with Tesla overstating just how capable of a system it is. That's not the case in South Korea, though, where the Texas-based automaker has allegedly vastly overstated the legality of FSD usage and charged customers for it nonetheless. Now, tens of thousands of Korean Tesla owners are looking for answers.

Tesla apparently markets FSD in South Korea despite the fact that it knows the majority of its cars can't legally use the program in the country, the complaint from an advocacy group alleges. That means it can't be activated on the car. Soon, the complaint will be filed with the Korean Fair Trade Commission, a consumer protection agency, according to Reuters . Tesla will have to answer for why it marketed FSD to prospective buyers for years, even collecting the $6,726 lump-sum payment required for activation, even though it couldn't legally be used.

Currently, just 20% of Teslas registered in South Korea can legally use FSD because they're built in the U.S., according to a preliminary testimony given by Tesla Korea country manager Seo Young-deuk last month. Those specific cars meet U.S. vehicle-safety standards that South Korea recognizes as part of a free trade agreement. The thing is, most Teslas on the road in South Korea are manufactured in China, where no such agreement exists. It was only recently that Tesla started the process of obtaining FSD certification on China-made vehicles, even though it has been charging customers for the software for over three years.

Right now, it's not totally clear how many customers in South Korea bought FSD subscriptions on ineligible vehicles, but the automaker has sold over 170,000 China-made vehicles in the country since 2023, Reuters reports. The company continued to market FSD as sales of ineligible China-manufactured vehicles surged in South Korea in recent years, and last year, 99% of new Teslas sold in the country couldn't legally use FSD.

The complaint alleges that last year, Tesla promoted FSD as "coming soon" and posted a demonstration video filmed in South Korea without clearly disclosing that the tech could only be used in a tiny fraction of the vehicles it was selling, according to Reuters . The consumer advocacy group accused Tesla Korea of deceptive marketing and has asked the KFTC to issue a temporary cease-and-desist order on marketing FSD for ineligible vehicles, impose fines and refer the case to state investigators.

It may be an uphill battle, though. Just last month, a court in Seoul dismissed a lawsuit filed by Tesla owners seeking refunds for the FSD option, Reuters reports. The court rejected the claim that Tesla had failed to deliver the driver-assistance system. Instead, it put the onus of the issue on regulatory and legal restrictions that had limited the company's ability to roll out future functions.

raw_title: These Are the Coolest and Craziest Cars We Saw at SEMA 2026
title: These Are the Coolest and Craziest Cars We Saw at SEMA 2026
raw_summary: It’s impossible to grasp the size of the SEMA show until you actually experience it. There are thousands of builds created by tens of thousands of dedicated enthusiasts excited to share their passion with the world. While we would love to spend the full week delving into each and every build, there simply isn’t enough time. So, we picked a few of our early favorites from this year’s show. Hopefully, you’ll find them as endearing as we do. Kei cars are already an adorable bunch, but add in Rocket Bunny’s Pandem Pocket Bunny kit, and now you’re talking best-in-show cute at your local car show. What you’re looking at here is a pair of Suzuki Twins built into R32 and R34 GT-Rs. These specific examples were built with no expense spared. The R32 makes around 120 horsepower from its turbocharged 1.0-liter, while the R34’s Twin was left more stock. – Jack Fitzgerald

I found this chopped-up Tesla Cybertruck parked in the back corner of the Central Hall, covered in Grand Theft Auto VI and Rockstar Games branding. Somehow, with a sports car figure and a giant APR spoiler, the Cybertruck’s styling looks good? – Carter Fry
Can’t help but grin looking at this track-spec first-gen Toyota Tacoma . Not pictured is the engine mounted out back in the bed, below the massive rear wing. – Carter Fry

No, you’re not looking at some AI hallucination of a Lexus pickup that doesn’t exist. This is the Meso Customs TX1, a legitimate Lexus pickup based on the Toyota Tacoma and built by the crew at Meso Customs. The front end takes on the look of a Lexus GX , and even the interior gets overhauled to look and feel like what you’d get from the luxury brand. – Jack Fitzgerald

There are plenty of ways to get your race car to the track, but most of them involve purpose-built haulers based on proven HD trucks. Builder Raymond Canales looked at the available options and said, “I can do better.” Then he set to work creating this tag-axle VW hauler based on the beloved Type 2, giving new meaning to its “Transporter” surname. Built specifically to transport his VW Beetle race car, the Type 2 Hauler is just the kind of inspired lunacy with a practical purpose that we can get behind. – Andrew Wendler

Mark Denlinger’s Mad Customs is responsible for this Chevy wagon build. While Nomads get most of the love, this 210 four-door wagon restomod features a natural patina to complement its subtle hardware updates. Yes, it’s lowered, but so deftly it almost appears to just be sitting on a worn suspension; the Forgeline EO1 wheels are painted black to keep a low profile; keep the hood closed, and you’d never see its LT4 GM V-8. Denlinger also fabbed up custom tubs to clear the rear tires and modified the cargo floor to clear the custom exhaust that was crafted in-house. With apologies to Michael Jackson, this is one smooth criminal—if you know where to look. – Andrew Wendler

Steve Stroppe has a history of clean builds, and this Z/28 does nothing to sully that legacy. Featuring a carbureted Chevy big-block and a massaged turbo-hydromantic 400 transmission with a Gear Vendors overdrive, it pays respect to builds of the past. But the craftsmanship is so meticulous, and the Ice Gray Metallic paint and Graphite Blue interior are so sublime, the whole thing makes a contemporary statement without trying too hard. The Camaro was basically the poster child for custom builds in the ‘80s and ‘90s, but for those of us raised in the Rust Belt, there’s still something special about a well-executed 1969 Z/28 project. – Andrew Wendler

raw_title: GM Recalls Over 67,000 Chevy Blazer EVs And Cadillac Lyriqs, Vistiqs, And Even Celestiqs For Temporary Loss Of Braking
title: Urgent Safety Alert: GM Recalls Over 67,000 Chevy Blazer EVs And Cadillac Lyriqs, Vistiqs, And Even Celestiqs For Temporary Loss Of Braking
raw_summary: General Motors is recalling 67,380 Chevrolet Blazer EVs And Cadillac Lyriqs , Vistiqs , and even Celestiqs because under specific circumstances, a software defect can cause a temporary loss of braking ability. According to the NHTSA recall report , GM is aware of 20 minor accidents due to the fault, two of which resulted in minor injuries. Fortunately, the condition only arises at low speeds, but any loss of braking is a deeply concerning and dangerous occurrence. Two-wheel-drive Cadillac Lyriqs are not included in the recall, and the only Blazer EV trims involved are SS and Police Pursuit Vehicles. Cadillac Lyriqs are hit hardest by the recall, which includes 474 2023 Lyriqs, 22,819 2024 Lyriqs, 11,926 2025 Lyriqs, 9,322 2026 Lyriqs, and 44 2027 Lyriqs. The recall also includes 13,627 2026 Vistiqs and 5,175 2027 Vistiqs, as well as 51 2025 Celestiqs, and 31 2026 Celestiqs. (This is one of our best glimpses yet into how many Celestiqs have been sold.) The only Chevrolets included in the recall are 562 2024 Blazer EVs, 2012 2025 Blazer EVs, 1,314 2026 Blazer EVs, and 23 2027 Blazer EVs. VINs are already searchable on NHTSA's website , and the remedy comes in the form of an over-the-air update for owners who have opted in to those, otherwise owners will have to take their vehicles to dealerships to have the software update downloaded.

The only Chevrolets included in the recall are 562 2024 Blazer EVs, 2012 2025 Blazer EVs, 1,314 2026 Blazer EVs, and 23 2027 Blazer EVs. VINs are already searchable on NHTSA's website , and the remedy comes in the form of an over-the-air update for owners who have opted in to those, otherwise owners will have to take their vehicles to dealerships to have the software update downloaded.

The conditions that lead to the temporary loss of brake function are very specific. According to the recall report and GM's testing, "when the brakes are lightly applied at low speeds during a sharp turn and the vehicle encounters a bump or depression – such as at the end of a driveway – a momentary release and reapplication of the brakes may cause the software's slip calculation to misinterpret wheel movement. In some instances, this may result in a temporary loss of braking. The phenomenon is unique to certain vehicles equipped with performance all-wheel drive (pAWD, RPO X0E) and is resolved when the brakes are applied again."

GM already recalled 21,469 all-wheel-drive Lyriqs for a similar issue in 2024 , but it found that vehicles built with the software changes following that recall and vehicles that already received the software update from that recall are still susceptible to the conditions described in the new recall, and they need the latest update. The latest software update corrects the slip calculation in the vehicle's brake system control module that causes the temporary loss of braking, which coincidentally is the same claim made on the 2024 recall. Hopefully this time it actually fixes the problem.

If you drive one of the cars included in the recall, be aware of the possibility of braking loss, and remember that if you experience braking loss, normal brake function should return on the next brake press. Dealers should already be notified of the recall, but owner notification is estimated to begin on December 14.

article_paragraphs: Oh, that's just $1 million worth of vehicles driving up those ramps

SEMA is one of the few places where a Lamborghini can struggle to stand out. Park one next to a row of wildly modified trucks, and it might barely earn a second glance. Elevation Off Grid (EOG) had a different idea, and frankly, it leverages the Lamborghini in question as more of a prop since the company is really selling the Super Duty trucks it's sitting on. So yeah, this is a sincerely impressive display for multiple reasons.

First, let's break this down a touch. Elevation Off Grid is known for building custom heavy-duty trucks that don't sacrifice their heavy-duty capabilities. EOG created a similar display at SEMA in the past, but with the Lamborghini thrown in the mix, the company estimates there's close to a $1 million elevated 11 feet off the Las Vegas Convention Center floor. Watching the setup of this display is what caught our eye in the first place. Some companies may have used some type of crane or forklift, but once the Lamborghini was loaded onto the Super Duty, ramps were used to drive the car-hauling rig atop the other two shot trucks. We can only imagine that a very confident — and well-insured — driver was piloting that white Ford Super Duty .

Sure, the stunt is cool, and again, it'll get the brand noticed, but there's a somewhat sad detail why this SEMA display caught our eye in the first place. For all the cool stuff we see at SEMA each year, plenty of the cars, trucks, and SUVs in question are little more than fancy rollers. Some don't even have complete powertrains, while others are running Bluetooth driveshafts. While they might look cool, they're often held together with hopes and dreams, and the flashier vehicles tend to be vaporware cars that you could only wish to life .

That's a big reason why this demo from EOG is so cool. Any company can talk a big game, but some actually back their products up. Very few can build a truck that shows off so many concurrent skills in one relatively simple-looking display. Driving a pickup onto ramps is ordinarily unremarkable. Doing it with a Lamborghini behind the cab and two other trucks waiting underneath adds a little more pressure to the job. This all could've been viral for a very different reason.

Then consider what the other two trucks are doing — they're supporting the weight of a custom Super Duty and a Lamborghini. Yes, they're sharing the load, but we're still talking about several thousand pounds on each pickup. The company boasts that its beds are capable of supporting 10,000 pounds (4,536 kg), so in theory, each is doing relatively light work. EOG then uses LiquidSpring Smart Suspension components to keep either truck from squatting under the load. It's a very clever way to make a very clear point.

raw_title: BMW Just Went 186 MPH In The New Alpina 7 Series
title: BMW Just Went 186 MPH In The New Alpina 7 Series
raw_summary: Thanks to spy shots, we already knew BMW was hard at work cooking up the next Alpina B7 and that it'll have a V8 that sounds pretty great . The brand has now come out with official footage of the car doing high-speed testing at the Nardò test track, exceeding 186 mph. What, did you think the special label version of BMW's flagship sedan would be slow? For reference, the last-gen Alpina B7 already had a top speed of 205 mph, so 186 was frankly table stakes. That said, the speed itself arguably isn't what BMW is flexing her — it's the peace with which that speed is achieved. "Speed has always been baked into the Alpina brand's DNA," said BMW Alpina vice president Oliver Viellechner. "However, we are not just interested in top speed alone. What matters is how natural, stable and confident it feels to drive at that speed." Internally, the brand apparently calls these cars "distance-shrinking" machines; autobahn weapons made to cover literal continents in great speed, style, and serenity.

Internally, the brand apparently calls these cars "distance-shrinking" machines; autobahn weapons made to cover literal continents in great speed, style, and serenity.

You might recognize the name Nardò, by the way, from "Nardo Gray," that primer-like paint color popularized by Audi. The Nardò Ring, a 7.8-mile test track in southern Italy owned by Porsche and shaped like a perfect circle, is where that comes from.

Other confirmed details now include Alpina-signature 20-spoke lightweight wheels (peeping at the sidewall shows a diameter of 22 inches) wearing specially made tires that feature an extra layer of foam inside allowing for peak high-speed stability and comfort. Four oval exhaust tips emit a "rich, deep sound," and BMW says max torque out of that V8 is available "across virtually the entire rev range," while engine management software and throttle mapping is tweaked for smoothness over aggression. Gearbox tuning, too, has been revised to accommodate the bump in horsepower and engine speeds.

This new B7 (or whatever BMW will choose to call the next Alpina-ized 7 Series) will be the first production car made under the joint BMW Alpina brand. BMW announced that it had acquired Alpina back in 2022, but didn't take full control over the tuner until the beginning of this year. The new BMW Alpina 7 Series will be unveiled next year.

article_paragraphs: Range Rover is pulling the plug on its two most affordable models, the Evoque and Velar, as a new entry-level EV steps in.
For decades, the Range Rover name was viewed as a status symbol, mostly used by wealthy buyers, high-powered executives, and even royalty.
That started to change with the launch of the Evoque in 2011 and the Velar in 2017, making the iconic British luxury brand a little more accessible.

In the US, the 2026 Range Rover Evoque starts at $49,900, and the Velar starts at $61,600. That’s considerably less than the Sport and flagship Range Rover SUVs, which start at $83,700 and $107,400, respectively.

Range Rover’s accessible luxury era is reportedly drawing to a close. Martin Limbert, Range Rover’s managing director, confirmed to Autocar that the Evoque and Velar will officially be discontinued, with production set to end in 2027.
While it has no direct replacement planned, the new Range Rover GT will serve as the brand’s new entry-level vehicle.
Range Rover revealed the GT in July, presenting it as the fifth and newest member of the lineup. Unlike the distinct SUV design Range Rover has built the brand on, the GT is a low-slung grand tourer.
The electric GT is “a captivating new expression” of the brand, Range said, describing it as “the most technologically sophisticated” model it’s ever designed.

title: Germany's EV share hits record 37% as BEVs beat gas and diesel combined
raw_summary: Battery-electric cars took a record 37% of Germany’s new car market in October, according to data released today by the Kraftfahrt-Bundesamt (KBA), the country’s federal motor vehicle authority. That’s 94,086 BEVs, up 79.5% from 52,425 a year earlier. For the second month in a row, German buyers registered more fully electric cars than gasoline and diesel cars combined. And with two months left in the year, Germany has already blown past the auto industry’s EV forecast for all of 2026.

article_paragraphs: Battery-electric cars took a record 37% of Germany’s new car market in October, according to data released today by the Kraftfahrt-Bundesamt (KBA), the country’s federal motor vehicle authority. That’s 94,086 BEVs, up 79.5% from 52,425 a year earlier.

For the second month in a row, German buyers registered more fully electric cars than gasoline and diesel cars combined. And with two months left in the year, Germany has already blown past the auto industry’s EV forecast for all of 2026.
The overall market barely grew in October. Total new car registrations rose 1.7% to 254,492 units, which means the EV growth came straight out of combustion cars.

Gasoline car registrations crashed 40.5% to 38,516 units, a 15.1% share. Diesel fell 21.6% to 23,882 units, or 9.4% of the market. Add them up and pure combustion cars made up just 24.5% of new registrations, 12.5 points less than BEVs alone.

Plug-in hybrids slipped 7.9% to 28,499 units (11.2%). So plug-ins accounted for about 48% of the German market last month, and the average CO2 emissions of new cars dropped 21.1% year-over-year to 79.4 g/km.

As we reported this summer, BEVs became the most popular powertrain in Germany for the first time in June with a 28.4% share. They’ve kept climbing every month since: 32.4% in August, 34.5% in September, and now 37% in October.

Through the first ten months of the year, Germany has registered 698,230 BEVs, up 60.7% year-over-year. That’s about 28.2% of the 2,476,290 new cars registered in 2026 so far, up from roughly 19% for the full year 2025.

And the industry didn’t see it coming. In December, the VDA, Germany’s auto industry association, forecast about 693,000 BEV registrations for all of 2026. Germany passed that in October. At the current pace, it’s on track for somewhere around 875,000 by the end of the year.

title: Waymo confirms it's shaking up its Uber relationship in January 2028
raw_summary: Waymo will end its exclusivity with Uber in the Austin and Atlanta markets starting in January 2028, co-CEO Tekedra Mawakana told Bloomberg News in a report published Wednesday. The robotaxi company will offer rides directly through its own smartphone app, like it does in other cities. Uber confirmed to TechCrunch Wednesday that it still plans to host Waymo robotaxis on its app for as long as the two companies agree. Waymo did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

article_paragraphs: Waymo will end its exclusivity with Uber in the Austin and Atlanta markets starting in January 2028, co-CEO Tekedra Mawakana told Bloomberg News in a report published Wednesday.

The robotaxi company will offer rides directly through its own smartphone app, like it does in other cities. Uber confirmed to TechCrunch Wednesday that it still plans to host Waymo robotaxis on its app for as long as the two companies agree. Waymo did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Mawakana’s comments come after reporting earlier this year by the Financial Times that Waymo was looking to get out of its deal with Uber, which was set to expire in May 2028 . Mawakana told Bloomberg that Waymo initially partnered with Uber because the ride-hail giant offered scale. But the experience for riders has been “a little bit of a crapshoot,” she said, especially because riders never know for sure if they’re going to hail a robotaxi or a human-driven car.
“It’s important for us to have that relationship with the rider. We’ve gotten that feedback from the riders in those markets,” Mawakana said.
Uber — which has many robotaxi and other autonomous vehicle partners — told Bloomberg that it was Waymo’s idea not to add an option in the ride-hail giant’s app to book a robotaxi directly.

title: Ford Says Even the Fathom EV's Fanciest Trims Will Stay Under $40K
raw_summary: Skeptics of the Ford Fathom EV pickup have questioned Ford’s ability to provide a sub-$30,000 truck since its introduction last year, but Andrew Frick, president of Ford’s Model e division, told the Detroit Free Press that even the top trim will remain below $40,000. After taking a prototype Fathom for a test drive last month, Ford CEO Jim Farley was reportedly blown away by the small truck’s handling and performance, calling it a “breakthrough product.” He also said the Fathom is on track to hit the market toward the end of 2027, though the team will need to keep developing at a rapid pace to get it out on time and within budget.

Ford announced the Fathom’s starting price in August. At $29,945, the pickup truck offers an affordable way to enter the EV world, and it’s the first to ride on Ford’s Universal Electric Vehicle (UEV) platform. The Fathom is already confirmed to be equipped with a touchscreen, built-in Apple Maps, Apple CarPlay, Android Auto, and Blue Cruise hands-free driving capabilities.

The UEV platform operates on a 400-volt electrical architecture, so charging won’t be as quick as vehicles that use an 800-volt system, but Ford says the trade-off for a lighter, more affordable vehicle is worth it. It’ll also use a 48-volt system instead of the traditional 12-volt system used in most vehicles; the higher voltage is intended to increase power and fuel efficiency. Farley revealed this week that the platform will break up the electrical components into five distinct zones to simplify production processes and reduce costs.

The Fathom’s starting price puts it on the more affordable end of the entire car market, including gas-powered and hybrid vehicles, but higher trim levels often bring a significantly higher price to a new car. Ford, however, is reportedly aiming to keep even the highest Fathom trim below $40,000. It’s unclear what will be included in the base model versus the higher specs, but top trims will likely have a longer range, among other upgrades.

The Fathom’s pre-order list is expected to open in the first quarter of 2027, and the truck is slated to go on sale in the last quarter of the year. Pricing beyond the Fathom’s entry point hasn’t yet been announced, but it seems even the highest trim will remain relatively affordable.

article_paragraphs: Voters delivered a stunning rebuke of Republicans and everything they stand for Tuesday night, taking control of both the House and the Senate in a wave of wins that just kept coming. Democrats kept winning, again and again, wave after wave. A bluekkake, if you will. And while that's great news for the stock market, the Middle East, healthcare, trans kids' safety, and so many other hugely important issues, voters also rejected Elon Musk and his billionaire meddling . We won't be able to get rid of him overnight, but at least Musk's dreams of a Tesla-SpaceX-Twitter-xAI merger are probably dead.

If you remember, Musk has long been reported to want his companies all under one roof to complete Tesla's tranformation into an AI/robotics company (or stop making cars without crashing the stock price). xAI already merged with Twitter and stuck Musk's antisemitism-spewing, CSAM-generating chatbot in Teslas , then merged with Spacex ahead of its IPO . As previously reported, Musk had then ordered Tesla to look at spinning off its China business to help his main division merge with SpaceX more easily. Musk also floated the possibility with investors, and one of the Trump administration's lasting legacies will be its love of corporate mergers, so it sounded plausible.

With Democrats winning control of both the House and the Senate, likely finishing with 258 Representatives and 55 (or 56!) Senators, the left doesn't just have power, it has a mandate from the voters to put a stop to everything the Trump administration is doing. Raskin will chair the House Judiciary Committee, Garcia will chair the House Oversight Committee, and both have promised investigations into any criminal activity that's taken place. That's not exactly fertile ground for a major corporate merger, especially after Musk attempted to inflame a race riot in Ireland, campaigned for Germany's Nazi-adjacent AfD party, and blew hundreds of millions of dollars trying to elect Republicans.

Yes, our friends over at the Tesla Takedown kept a running thread going last night, highlighting every race Musk lost and how much money he wasted. Nearly two dozen races, all won by Dems, even though a Republican billionaire tried to buy their elections. Per Vanity Fair , Musk dumped an eye-watering $474 million into this election, and he still got kicked in the nards. He could have given $50,000 to 9,400 people and still wasted less of his money.

Democrats who haven't been bought off by the crypto and AI lobbies have been sounding the alarm in recent months about the dangers of any one person having as much power as Elon does. The man has the power to slow down Ukraine's military's internet , and the prospect of combining SpaceXAI with the most valuable car company in the world makes a lot of regulators nervous. Expect it to be a fight with the centrists in the party, but Dems are more likely to try to weaken Musk's power, not hand him a win.

Because our election system is weird, Republicans won't lose power until January and could theoretically rush the merger through. But even the Motley Fool — a website that published " Prediction: SpaceX Stock Will Go Parabolic After Nov. 6 " the day both Tesla and SpaceX shares plunged — doesn't think that's likely. In an article foolishly calling the merger "inevitable ," the MFers timeline is still "within the next 12 months" not "before January." They also admit many factors, including antitrust enforcement could be a problem for the merger.

With Dems winning a huge mandate to govern, Republican politicians should be less willing to stick their necks out for that eternally sticky loser, too, so calling it "inevitable" is certainly a take. More importantly, Republicans have a much more important activity on their agenda than facilitating this merger. With Trump humiliated and unable to run for a third term anyway, Republicans are leaderless. When they move from depression to anger, they're going to start pointing fingers. Infighting and power struggles are inevitable unless Republicans just give up completely.

With Tucker Carlson and Marjorie Taylor-Greene-whatever waiting in the wings, the far-right giving up isn't likely either. So expect Republicans to be distracted, Democrats to feel emboldened, Jeffries and Schumer to remain spineless cowards, and Elon Musk to struggle getting any attempt at a Tesla-SpaceX merger off the ground. That's probably something Elon's sad about, but for the rest of us, it can only be good news any time Elon's dreams go up in smoke.

Ferrari made the announcement that its first all-electric vehicle was sold out through '27 during its earnings call earlier this week, according to InsideEVs . The news comes after a July announcement from the automaker that the $560,800 EV had already hit its 2026 sales target after being available for purchase for just a couple of months. People want this thing, and people want pronouns in email signatures again. It's morning again in America.

"The Luce that we plan to sell next year basically are all allocated," Benedetto Vigna, Ferrari CEO, said in the earnings call, according to InsideEVs, adding that customers who placed an order now would have to wait a year to actually take delivery. Hopefully this isn't an empty promise, like "gas prices are going to come down after the midterms." Anyway, Ferrari hasn't said how many Luces it plans to sell, and it hasn't provided any sort of regional breakdown of orders so far.

Like Jon Ossoff and his lightning-fast election night, Ferrari made quick work of its 2026 sales goal. Two unnamed sources told the Financial Times that the automaker planned to sell just under 500 examples of the Jony Ive-designed EV this year, and doing it in such a quick fashion is quite the indictment on what the average internet car enthusiast thinks a popular car should be. Long term, Ferrari says it wants to sell about 2,500 Luces by 2030, or roughly 600 per year, though the exact ramp-up numbers haven't been released yet.

When the Luce first launched, you'd be hard-pressed to find a fan. Folks didn't like its looks, the fact it was a sedan, or the EV-ness of it all. People who never thought about cars were letting the takes fly , but Ferrari has remained steadfast. It has defended the Luce, attempting to showcase its new tech while also reaching the next generation of wealthy buyers in China and other tech hubs like Silicon Valley. Basically, they're targeting folks who are already driving EVs but are looking for something more premium.

Still, this hasn't stopped people, even though with close ties to Ferrari, from throwing hissy fits over the Luce. When the car first launched, we reported that Ferrari's former longtime CEO, Luca di Montezemolo , told reporters that if he were to say what he really thought about the Luce, he'd "be doing Ferrari a disservice" and it risked "destroying a legend." He even said that he hoped Ferrari would "at least remove the prancing horse from that car."
In any case, it's time to jump in the Luce, crank up "Fight Song" and blast down the highway, because we're libbing out in this bih.

Walkable communities are as old as the hills. That’s what people did before automobiles hit the scene and cities were organized around cars. Credit for applying the walkability model to 21st century urban planning goes to the Franco-Colombian scientist Carlos Moreno, who formalized the 15 Minute City concept in 2016. The idea got a further boost of attention when the Mayor of Paris, Anne Hidalgo, pitched walkable, bike-able neighborhoods as part of her successful re-election campaign in 2020.

The COVID-19 lockdown of 2020 was also a pivotal moment, with a surge in work-from-home households drawing attention to the need for local resources as a matter of survival and resiliency in case of a widespread emergency.

The 15 Minute City model covers a lot of ground, but the basic idea is that people should be able to do their shopping, recreation, socializing, and other essential routines within walking or biking distance from their homes, making cars largely optional within the neighborhood. Walkable access to schools and health care is also part of the plan.

The argument for 15-minute cities (also called 15-minute neighborhoods or 15-minute communities) is also pretty straightforward. Walking is healthier than sitting in a car. Avoiding injury or death from car accidents is another plus. Walking also reduces carbon emissions, and it saves money on gas.

In addition, walkability levels the playing field, so to speak. Everyone in the 15-minute zone has walkable access to basic resources, regardless of whether or not they can afford a car. In other words, there is a significant equity and inclusion element to the concept…

…and, that’s where the trouble kicks in. In 2022 the World Economic Forum posted an article by Lisa Chamberlain, the founder of the urban communications and business firm Strategies for City Builders. Chamberlain describes a 15 Minute City as characterized by diversified, mixed-use neighborhoods built to withstand shocks like COVID-19 and climate change.

title: SpaceX Starship Will Need To Re-Fuel 22 Times In Space To Make It To The Moon
raw_summary: As NASA plans to send astronauts back to the surface of the Moon in 2028 , there's still the small matter of figuring out how to get them there. While the Artemis II mission proved that we can send people around the Moon and bring them safely home, the space agency needs a way to take astronauts out of the Orion capsule and down to the actual ground. The original plan was for a SpaceX Starship to fulfill this duty, and that could still be the case. But delays in the development of that ambitious rocket caused NASA to re-open the contract, which allowed Blue Origin to toss its hat in the ring . Still, SpaceX insists it will fend off this challenge from a rival billionaire-owned space company and win the contract all over again. The only thing standing in its way: the minor fact that it has to refuel the Starship in-orbit, something never done before and that SpaceX hasn't even attempted yet. Oh, and it has to do it many, many times. How many? Great question. The NASA Aerospace Safety Advisory Panel recently announced that, by their calculations, a Starship would require fully 22 in-orbit refuelings to get that one single rocket to the Moon's surface, per Ars Technica . Again, the total number of times that any rocket has ever done this is zero. Specifically, the plan from SpaceX is to launch one Starship into orbit to act as a fuel depot; then launch many other Starships to load up that first one with fuel; then launch a final Starship to take on that fuel from the depot and head out to the Moon.
